source.title: On the Trajectories of SGD Without Replacement

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports gradient-based training trajectories on synthetic neural-network tasks, but does not measure the classification-error outcomes or specific conditions named by V1–V6.
record.gate_note: The paper reports two synthetic ReLU-network experiments in which SGD without replacement escapes a spurious local minimum. These are MSE results, not benchmark training-classification-error results; the paper does not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study's own results concern implicit regularization and escape from stationary regions under SGD without replacement. It does not test any listed version: its ReLU experiments do not vary teacher-student width, and its stability argument concerns mini-batch SGD rather than V5's full-batch edge-of-stability behavior or recovery above the initial stability limit.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors attribute lower-variance trajectories and faster traversal of flat regions to a drift caused by dependent batches. They explicitly do not establish a general characterization of the minima reached or a general convergence guarantee.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes SGD without replacement and compares it with GD and SGD with replacement; the reported synthetic experiments use shallow ReLU networks and MSE, rather than the benchmark classification recipes in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The synthetic comparison varies batch size (1 versus 2) in Fig. 6; the paper states that SGD without replacement escapes local minima in both settings.

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic shallow-ReLU MSE tasks, SGD without replacement escapes a spurious minimum reached by GD. Compared with replacement sampling, it escapes faster with smaller oscillations; both reach a global minimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD sampling without replacement can accelerate escape along flat regions of spurious minima on synthetic shallow-ReLU regression tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 8 gives conditions under which the additional expected regularization step of SGD without replacement exceeds the corresponding GD displacement. Section 7.3 explicitly lists cases where this cannot explain avoidance of the stability edge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under local expansion and covariance conditions with at least two sufficiently large Hessian eigenvalues, reshuffling-induced drift can dominate GD displacement and may explain SGD's departure from GD trajectories.

record.problems: The experiments are synthetic and use MSE; the reported outcomes are qualitative, with no uncertainty estimates. They do not measure the classification-error behavior in the claim versions.

untested.parts: CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and model-size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, failure frequencies from standard initialization, jointly increasing widths, and adding student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, special initialization, or normalization.
Initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, learning speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery or divergence above the initial linearized stability limit, and full-batch sharpness and loss trajectories near the stability threshold.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The stability observations about full-batch GD are attributed to earlier work, not newly measured here. The conditional SGD argument does not challenge V5's explicitly full-batch statement. Appendix K states that figure-generating code is available, contrary to the record's code_released field.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model size, early stopping, and the specified recipes.
Teacher-student widths, spurious-minimum frequency as widths grow, and the effect of giving the student extra neurons.
Plain versus residual network depth and training error; the specified shortcut, initialization, and normalization comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and very deep plain-network training.
Training outcomes and curvature behavior above or near the stability limit, including divergence conditions.
Batch-normalization comparisons for speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual-network training without normalization.
